name: Fibrodysplasia Ossificans Progressiva

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: Clinical Diagnostic Criteria for Fibrodysplasia Ossificans Progressiva

criteria.description: Congenital malformation of the great toes (hallux valgus or monophalangism)
Progressive heterotopic ossification in characteristic anatomic patterns involving soft tissues
Presence of pathogenic mutation in the ACVR1 gene
Recurrent painful soft tissue swellings (flare-ups) preceding ossification

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Presence of congenital great toe malformation plus progressive heterotopic ossification
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Genetic testing for ACVR1 mutation confirms diagnosis but is not mandatory if clinical criteria are met.

pathognomonic.symptomName: Congenital malformation of the great toes
pathognomonic.notes: Hallux valgus or monophalangism present at birth
searchTerms: abnormal big toe shape present at birth

pathognomonic.symptomName: Progressive heterotopic ossification of soft tissues
pathognomonic.notes: Ectopic bone formation in muscles, tendons, and ligaments
searchTerms: gradual abnormal bone growth in soft tissue
bone forming in muscles and skin

common.notes: Due to progressive ossification and ankylosis

occasional.notes: Due to ossification around middle ear structures
Caused by ossification of masticatory muscles

rare.notes: Secondary to restrictive chest wall disease

laboratory: Inflammatory markers may be elevated during flare-ups
imaging: Radiographs showing heterotopic ossification in characteristic patterns
CT or MRI to assess extent of soft tissue ossification
genetic: Pathogenic mutation in ACVR1 gene (most commonly c.617G>A; R206H)
other: Physical examination revealing malformed great toes
Clinical history of progressive ossification and flare-ups

distinguishingFeatures: Heterotopic ossification begins in skin and subcutaneous tissues
Non-progressive and limited to injury site

redFlags: Rapidly progressive heterotopic ossification causing joint ankylosis
Respiratory distress due to chest wall restriction
Flare-ups triggered by trauma or intramuscular injections
references: Kaplan FS, Shore EM. Fibrodysplasia ossificans progressiva: diagnosis, management, and therapeutic horizons. Pediatr Endocrinol Rev. 2008;6 Suppl 1:319-25.
Shore EM, Kaplan FS. Insights from a rare genetic disorder of extraskeletal bone formation, fibrodysplasia ossificans progressiva (FOP). Bone. 2011;49(1):4-7.
